newsitem.title: GERMANY: Steadier coffee prices leave German buyers cold.
newsitem.headline: Steadier coffee prices leave German buyers cold.

text.p: Firmer outright coffee prices as a result of dollar/mark and futures gains and steadier origin differentials were ignored by well-covered northern European buyers, German traders said on Monday.
"Consumers are still on year-end holidays or busy paying bills and planning the new year," one said.
"With cover stretching into the summer, it's hard to impress on them the need to watch potentially rising New York futures, where fund interest is still strong."
Traders said North American roasters may buy relatively more arabicas over the next fortnight than Europeans because their cover was less comfortable.
Sentiment here was also depressed by weak retail sales of roasted coffee after consumers had taken advantage of special Christmas offers to hoard some coffee.
Traders therefore saw no scope for retail price rises from the pre-Christmas lows.

The average German retail price declined to 6.80 marks per 0.5 kg from 7.40 marks in the course of 1996 although raw materials prices increased by 16 percent amid global tightness, statistics from the DKV coffee industry association showed.
Importers offered Brazils at $115-120 fob per 50 kg afloat compared with $114 in the week before Christmas, with supplies from local stocks at $120/125.
Traders said Brazilian shippers were unwilling to sell beyond Jan/Feb.
Colombians were at $150 compared with $137 previously and Central Americans were also described as firm, with Guatemalan and Costa Rican differentials pegged at 10 cents per lb over futures.
